summary.headline: Groww's Q2 FY27 call centred on Cost to Serve rising on AI compute, one-time INR10-13 crore hit, and MTF book adding ~INR600-700 crore a quarter.
summary.overview: Management explained that Cost to Serve rose in Q2 due to AI-related costs, higher compute on more trading days, and a one-time INR10-13 crore hit from delayed files on an expiry day. Cost to Grow fell because the IPL branding spend in Q1 did not recur. Management said the margin trading facility (MTF) book adds about INR600-700 crore a quarter on average, with volatility from stock-level moves and policy changes such as higher haircuts on crowded stocks. Other operating income rose on about 30 IPOs (including SBI AMC and NSE) and BSDA income. Management said the call was qualitative on several items, such as US stocks timing and UPI MDR outcome, and gave few new numbers on AUM or market share.

segments.name: Broking (cash and derivatives)
segments.commentary: Management said revenue in derivatives and commodities is driven by order count at INR20 per order, while cash revenue depends on both order size and count (lower of 10 bps or INR20). Cash market share has been about 15% and derivatives about 11% over the last three to four quarters, per analyst. August was the lowest volume month of Q2.

segments.name: Wealth (Groww Prime, MF Prime, Fisdom)
segments.commentary: Wealth AUM was disclosed for the first time; management said MF Prime is small. Users rose by almost 50% quarter-on-quarter, mainly from Groww Prime per analyst. Wealth income is reported within other operating income, and Fisdom users are now included in active customers.

segments.name: Lending (MTF, personal loans, loan against shares)
segments.commentary: MTF book adds about INR600-700 crore a quarter. Loan against shares was launched in the last two quarters with good early traction; personal loan book is growing gradually quarter-on-quarter. No figures were given for the lending book size.

segments.name: Other operating income
segments.commentary: Rose sequentially on about 30 IPOs in the quarter (including SBI AMC and NSE) and BSDA income. IPO and BSDA income were regrouped out of stocks revenue.

guidance_outlook: Cost to Grow for FY27 is expected to stay in the INR400-500 crore a year range, with more spend in good markets and less in weak ones.
Management expects the MTF book to keep growing, adding about INR600-700 crore a quarter, and MTF share of cash turnover to rise over time.
Management expects the CAS rule change to normalise volumes, with faster recovery depending on the effective date, which was awaited.
Management expects UPI MDR outcome to be not materially cost-changing, but the cap level (INR300 mentioned) is still under discussion with the regulator.
Management expects long-term convergence of cash and F&O market share toward NSE active share, but said this could take around 10 years.
capex_capacity: Management said 915 power-trading tools and web-based trading are not yet a material contributor to volume or revenue.
AI spend is rising: in-house AI stack being built to lower per-token cost; AI-related costs and compute costs rose in Q2.
Compute cost scales with trading days; management uses more compute on trading days and much less on non-trading days.
Company said the wealth integration (Fisdom) is complete and some products are being mainstreamed across apps.
demand_pricing: Management said competitive pricing approach is to give customers more value than they are charged, and it is not following competitors on price.
Analyst noted some discount brokers cut brokerage by half; management did not directly address this.
Volumes were affected by the CAS circular; management expects CAS changes to normalise volumes, with derivatives largely unaffected by the proposed options.
Customers using more than two products exceed 50%; over 5% use more than four products.
US stocks product is in early beta testing with good customer feedback; no timeline for full launch was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Cost to Grow fall sharply while Cost to Serve rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost to Grow fell because the Q1 IPL branding cost did not recur. Cost to Serve rose on AI-related costs, higher compute on more trading days, and a one-time INR10-13 crore hit from delayed expiry-day files.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a one-off MTF cost in September, as in March?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no one-off cost as such, though MTF costs were present. Policy changes now include higher haircuts (up to 80% on some crowded stocks) and more frequent approved-list reviews, including industry-level book checks.

qa_highlights.question: Why is order per ADTV rising while broking revenue is flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Derivatives and commodity revenue is per order, not per ADTV, and cash revenue depends on the asset mix (ETFs vs small caps). Ticket size shifts drive the difference, and cash brokerage per order is about INR15-16 versus INR20 in F&O.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the NSE active market share not reflected in cash and F&O market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects convergence over the long term as customers age and trade more and MTF grows, but noted it will not be quarter-to-quarter and may take about 10 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UPI MDR impact on cost to serve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still awaiting the final outcome. It expects no material cost change, but the cap (INR300 discussed) is critical and the company will push to lower it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost to grow run-rate for H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said around INR125 crore is the current average; H2 spend will depend on market conditions, with more spend if markets do well and less in weak markets.

risks_watch: SEBI's CAS circular outcome and effective date, which affects volume normalisation.
MTF book volatility from crowded stocks and possible haircut changes, plus policy execution risk.
Rising AI and compute costs within Cost to Serve, and the one-time INR10-13 crore hit recurring.
UPI MDR pricing outcome and cap level, which could affect transaction costs.
Competitive pressure from brokerage cuts and AI-led tools; US stocks product still in beta.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and product direction, but cautious and sometimes evasive on specifics: management declined to give a full launch timeline for US stocks, withheld MTF and wealth AUM breakdowns, and said UPI MDR and CAS outcomes were still pending.
key_quotes: And what we are seeing is on average we are able to add like INR600 crores, INR700 crores on a quarterly basis.
We don't want to force customer or push customers to use multiple products.
Cost to Serve primarily has costs related to transactions and costs related to technology from our side, whereas Cost to Grow is primarily a growth-related cost.

growth.why: No revenue growth guidance was given; management guided only to Cost to Grow of INR400-500 crore for FY27 and MTF book additions of INR600-700 crore a quarter, with no capacity additions and qualitative backing (MTF book growth, cash/F&O share stable near 15%/11%).
